summary: CCC-built stone lookout (1937-1939) in Great Smoky Mountains National Park; little used for detection, abandoned in the 1960s, and restored from 1995.

facts.design: two-story octagonal stone structure built from materials on the site
facts.status_note: The most recent visit account I read is a 2016 hike that describes the tower. I could not confirm its condition after 2016.

staffing.status: not staffed; abandoned as a lookout

access.note: Reached on foot through Great Smoky Mountains National Park, near the Appalachian Trail. I found no closure notice, but I did not read the park's current trail or tower notices.

visit.trail_note: The 2016 Friends of the Smokies classic hike to the tower covered 11.4 miles round trip.

events.note: Built 1937-1939 by the Civilian Conservation Corps from materials on the site; the register gives the span rather than one year
Restoration in 1995 was the first project of the Friends of the Smokies, which was created in 1993

corrections.why: The register and the 2012 FFLA report both give construction over 1937-1939, not a single year.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 2023 restoration (A Forever Places crew) and the 1995 'work finished a few years later' are not in any page I read, so they are left out. The Mountain Press restoration article returned HTTP 429 and was not read. Staffing years and any fires the tower spotted are not in these sources. Access is rated public as a hiking destination; climbing rules were not verified. A tnlandforms listing puts the peak in Haywood County, NC, which conflicts with the register's Cocke County, TN; the story does not mention a county. Used 1 WebSearch call and 6 page reads (one returned HTTP 429).
